facts.label: Leverage and cover
facts.text: Leverage on the last twelve months to 30 June 2026 is 9.38x total debt to Adjusted EBITDA and 10.46x on reported EBITDA; net of cash the figures are 9.03x and 10.07x. facts.label: Leverage and cover
facts.text: Cash interest cover is 1.40x on Adjusted EBITDA and 1.25x on reported EBITDA for the last twelve months, against 1.28x and 1.23x for 2025. Cover is thin because the August 2025 refinancing swapped USD 2.0 billion of 5.125% and 9.000% secured notes for USD 2.05 billion of 7.125% and 7.500% secured notes, which lifted the weighted average cost of debt from 7.4% to 7.6% between the 2024 and 2025 year-ends, and cash interest stays near USD 390 million a year while Adjusted EBITDA is only about 1.4 times that. A shortfall in EBITDA therefore falls straight onto liquidity, not onto a cushion. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against caution is that creditors were asked, and consented, before closing: the requisite holders and lenders approved the change-of-control amendments, the receivables facility will be extended to five years from completion with commitments raised from USD 200.0 million to USD 250.0 million, and the company has no dividend history in the documents supplied. These facts point to a negotiated, creditor-visible transaction rather than a surprise. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: - Leverage, not liquidity, is the binding constraint. Total debt is 9.38x Adjusted EBITDA and 10.46x reported EBITDA, cash interest of about USD 390 million costs 7.64% of debt and absorbs 71.67% of Adjusted EBITDA, and free cash flow after interest and capital expenditure is only about USD 84 million. A fall of 15.48% in Adjusted EBITDA removes it, and a fall of 28.33% leaves earnings equal to cash interest. Debt barely moved (up 0.09% from year-end 2025), so the improvement from 10.11x came from earnings and stays hostage to the advertising cycle, not to repayment. Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C14; Financial foundation (CP-1)

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest case for a better view is that earnings are compounding while debt is flat: revenue grew 10.17% in the first half of 2026 and Adjusted EBITDA for the last twelve months is 7.82% above 2025, no debt matures for about 17 months, and the Merger arrives with creditor consents, a receivables facility to be extended to five years from completion and conditional redemption notices already issued for USD 1.8 billion of unsecured notes. If earnings kept growing at the recent pace with debt unchanged, leverage would keep falling without any refinancing. Basis: calculation C14; calculation C9; calculation C16; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cco-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; Business & governance (CP-1A)

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view

facts.label: Company and ownership
facts.text: The company sells advertising on roadside billboards, street furniture and airport displays, almost entirely in the United States, and about 75% of revenue comes from the America segment and about 25% from Airports. Most advertising is sold in four-week periods, so revenue reprices quickly in both directions, while contracts for sites, street furniture and airports run for years with minimum fees, so costs are slow to move. The mix gives short revenue visibility and a long fixed commitment, which is why modest revenue declines hit free cash flow quickly. facts.label: Competitive forces and external factors
facts.text: Rivalry is moderate: the United States outdoor industry is fragmented, with Lamar and Outfront among its other large operators and many local ones, and competition turns on audience reach, location quality and measurable results; the company can manage rates when demand rises because inventory is limited, which supports margin in an upswing but gives no protection in a downturn. New entrants face high barriers, because federal, state and local rules limit new billboard inventory and airport, transit and street furniture rights sit in exclusive contracts, which supports franchise value and recovery prospects but exposes the company to rebid risk when contracts expire. Substitutes are the main long-run threat, since outdoor advertising is only 2.3% of United States advertising spend and competes with digital media, while an outside forecast the company cites expects outdoor revenue to grow 4.0% a year from 2026 to 2030. Buyers are diversified and short-term, which lowers concentration risk and shortens visibility; suppliers, meaning landlords and authorities, hold the stronger hand because lease and concession cost is a very large expense and partly fixed. facts.label: Outlook
facts.text: Over the next twelve to twenty-four months the near-term outlook is supportive but unproven: first-half revenue growth of 10.17% and rising margin favour a further fall in leverage if debt stays flat, no debt matures, and the Merger caps new borrowing until it closes; headwinds are the cash cost of the Merger, a seasonally weak first quarter that leaves debt service resting on the lowest earnings of the year, and elevated interest rates. Over three to five years the outlook depends on the 2028 and 2029 refinancing and on whether the acquirer adds or removes debt; a sector tailwind is the outside forecast of 4.0% annual growth in outdoor revenue to 2030, which is the company's cited view and not tested here. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: A realistic downside starts with an advertising slowdown that cuts revenue across both segments and a fall in air travel that hits Airports. Because most advertising is sold in four-week blocks, revenue falls within a quarter, while site lease minimums and concession fees do not, so Adjusted EBITDA falls by more than revenue; a fall of 15.48% in Adjusted EBITDA removes free cash flow, and a fall of 20% turns it negative at about USD 25 million with cover of 1.12x. The gap is funded from cash and undrawn availability of about USD 398 million, which lasts about one year of cash interest, so liquidity is not distressed in 2027 but the 2028 notes would have to be refinanced with cover near 1.12x, at a time when the cost of that debt is likely higher than the average of 7.64%. Management can cut capital expenditure, which was 3.85% of revenue in 2025, and apply Spain proceeds to debt, subject to the Merger. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress through 2027 but not sufficient to refinance 2028 on current terms without a recovery or sponsor support. Basis: calculation C5; calculation C7; calculation C11; calculation C6; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cco-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 9

facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Clear Channel Outdoor Holdings presents an adequate business profile supported by a regulated United States franchise, rising digital revenue and firm recent growth, but credit quality is constrained by leverage of 9.38x Adjusted EBITDA and thin cash interest cover of 1.40x. Cash-flow durability appears weak because free cash flow is about USD 84 million, which a fall of 15.48% in Adjusted EBITDA removes. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on earnings growth, on whether the Merger completes and on how the acquirer finances the redemption of the 2028 and 2029 unsecured notes. The primary downside path is an advertising downturn that reaches earnings through fixed site costs and meets the 2028 maturities with little cushion. Further analysis would require the acquirer's financing, a management projection and covenant workings. Top risk: refinancing the 2028 and 2029 maturities after an earnings downturn. Basis: calculation C1; calculation C8; calculation C5; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

## Request

Financial foundation for Clear Channel Outdoor Holdings, Inc. (issuer id cco), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the issuer's statements, debt, leverage, cash interest cover and liquidity inputs from the seven supplied documents, as reported on a continuing-operations basis in USD.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Leverage is very high: on the last twelve months to 30 June 2026, total debt is 9.38x Adjusted EBITDA and 10.46x reported EBITDA, while cash interest cover is only 1.40x on Adjusted EBITDA, so creditors depend on refinancing access rather than internally generated cash.
Basis: calculation C32; calculation C29; calculation C34; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cco-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2

Near-term funding is not the constraint: undrawn facilities of USD 205.5 million sit beside cash and about USD 197 million of cash interest expected in the second half of 2026, and no note or loan matures before 2028. Reported EBITDA is derived here as operating income plus depreciation and amortization because the company states none, and cash flows mix continuing and discontinued operations, so cover and free cash flow carry that qualification.
Basis: calculation C48; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cco-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cco-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 117; calculation C1
### Leverage and cover

Leverage on the last twelve months to 30 June 2026 is 9.38x total debt to Adjusted EBITDA and 10.46x on reported EBITDA; net of cash the figures are 9.03x and 10.07x. Year-end 2025 stood at 10.11x and 10.51x, so the improvement comes from earnings, with Adjusted EBITDA up 7.82% over FY2025 while total debt rose only 0.09%, rather than from repayment. FY2024 looks worse at 11.90x and 12.49x, but that year's debt still includes the term loan of the former Europe-North business whose earnings are outside the continuing figures, so the true improvement is smaller than the headline.
Basis: calculation C32; calculation C26; calculation C20; calculation C50; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 101

Cash interest cover is 1.40x on Adjusted EBITDA and 1.25x on reported EBITDA for the last twelve months, against 1.28x and 1.23x for 2025. Cover is thin because the August 2025 refinancing swapped USD 2.0 billion of 5.125% and 9.000% secured notes for USD 2.05 billion of 7.125% and 7.500% secured notes, which lifted the weighted average cost of debt from 7.4% to 7.6% between the 2024 and 2025 year-ends, and cash interest stays near USD 390 million a year while Adjusted EBITDA is only about 1.4 times that. A shortfall in EBITDA therefore falls straight onto liquidity, not onto a cushion.
Basis: calculation C34; calculation C31; calculation C8; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 73; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 102
### Cash flow quality

Free cash flow after cash interest is positive but small: operating cash flow of USD 160.374 million less capital expenditure of USD 76.122 million leaves USD 84.252 million for the last twelve months, 1.65% of total debt, against USD 31.981 million for 2025 and a deficit of USD 62.649 million for 2024. The figures combine continuing and discontinued operations because the cash flow statement does not separate them. Operating cash flow is stated after operating lease cash payments of USD 105.949 million (net of interest) in the first half of 2026 and after USD 12.2 million of Merger transaction costs paid in the same half, the latter being one-off in nature.
Basis: calculation C12; calculation C52; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cco-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cco-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 33
### Liquidity and maturities

At 30 June 2026 cash of USD 192.138 million and USD 205.5 million of undrawn facility availability total USD 397.638 million against about USD 197 million of cash interest expected in the second half of 2026. No note or loan matures before 2028, when USD 1,324.631 million falls due, almost all of it the 2028 senior notes and the term loan. Availability under the receivables facility is capped by a borrowing base tied to receivables, and the revolver letter of credit of USD 7.0 million that related to the Spain business was cancelled on 4 August 2026.
Basis: calculation C48; calculation C51; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cco-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cco-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 117
### Funding float and leases

Deferred revenue rose by USD 27.293 million to USD 102.73 million between year-end 2025 and 30 June 2026, a customer prepayment float that supports cash until the campaigns run. Operating lease liabilities of USD 1,361.914 million at 30 June 2026 sit outside total debt while the related site lease cost is inside EBITDA, so leverage here is not lease-adjusted and a lease-adjusted view would be materially higher.
Basis: calculation C46; calculation C47; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cco-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2

## Findings
### Bottom line

Creditors face an ownership change they cannot yet price: a pending take-private by funds advised by Mubadala Capital, with creditors' change-of-control protection waived, while the acquirer's financing and sponsor behaviour are not disclosed, so governance risk is Medium on incomplete evidence.

Operating leverage is real: site lease cost of USD 624.2 million was 38.91% of 2025 revenue and is partly fixed by minimum guarantees, while no single advertiser is material and digital reached 44.1% of revenue. Board composition, ownership above 5% and the Merger financing are not in the documents supplied.
### Key findings

- The Merger changes who controls the issuer without, on the documents supplied, changing who is owed what: the secured notes and credit agreements were amended so that the Merger is not a change of control, the amendments become operative only on completion, and conditional redemption notices cover the 2028 and 2029 senior notes. Creditors have already consented, so the protection they would normally hold on a takeover is gone, while the size and ranking of the acquirer's own debt are not established.

- Ownership is dispersed today and the future owner is only partly identified. The company has one hundred and sixty-one holders of record and no holder above 5% is named in the documents supplied, and the consortium is described with TWG Global in the annual report and the first-quarter documents but without it in the second-quarter documents. At the deal price the equity is worth about USD 1,236.9 million on shares outstanding at 30 June 2026, against company-defined net debt of USD 4,915.49 million, so debt is 79.90% of implied enterprise value and the creditors, not the shareholders, carry most of the claim.
Basis: calculation C2; calculation C3; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 51; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cco-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 8

- Governance disclosure is adequate for monitoring but silent on control rights. The auditor gave unqualified opinions on the statements and on internal control, covenant compliance is stated every quarter, and the Merger Agreement bars dividends and new borrowing without the acquirer's consent, which protects creditors until closing; directors, fees and related-party dealings are not in the documents supplied.

- Financial policy has favoured creditors on deleveraging but not on cost. Disposals of the international businesses raised USD 607.8 million in 2025, USD 375.0 million of which prepaid the term loan of a former subsidiary, and the company repurchased USD 229.7 million of senior notes at a discount, yet the August 2025 refinancing lengthened maturities at a higher weighted average cost of debt (7.6% against 7.4%). No dividend has been paid and none is intended.

Basis: calculation C6; calculation C7; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 66; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 67; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 73; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 102; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 51

- The business is a fixed-cost concession model with long commitments. Street furniture contracts run five to fifteen years and airport concessions five to ten, awarded by competitive bid with minimum fees, and the New York transit contract alone carries USD 390.0 million of minimum lease payments over fifteen years. That locks in cost and creates renewal risk, but digital growth and low advertiser concentration support revenue visibility.
- Seasonality is steep and favours the fourth quarter: Q1 2025 Adjusted EBITDA was 48.19% of Q4 2025, which leaves first-quarter debt service resting on the weakest earnings of the year.
Basis: calculation C8; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against caution is that creditors were asked, and consented, before closing: the requisite holders and lenders approved the change-of-control amendments, the receivables facility will be extended to five years from completion with commitments raised from USD 200.0 million to USD 250.0 million, and the company has no dividend history in the documents supplied. The Merger Agreement also bars new borrowing and dividends until closing, and stockholders approved it on 12 May 2026. These facts point to a negotiated, creditor-visible transaction rather than a surprise.

The view would move to Low if the acquirer's debt financing, equity contribution and the treatment of the 2028 and 2029 senior notes were disclosed and left secured creditors no worse placed, and it would move to High if the financing primed existing secured debt or distributions were funded from the company. Completion or termination of the Merger, which the documents supplied do not reach, would replace the public-company governance assessed here, with four days to the outside date from the as-of date.
Basis: calculation C9; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cco-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 34
### Limitations

- Directors, executive compensation and beneficial ownership are incorporated by reference to a later amendment of the annual report that is not supplied, so the conclusion that control is dispersed rests on the holder count alone and could change if a large holder exists.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 135; Source readiness (CP-0)

- Nothing after 5 August 2026 is supplied, so the conclusion that the Merger is pending may be out of date; completion would make the public-company governance assessed here obsolete and the sponsor assessment then applicable.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_cco-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 39; Source readiness (CP-0)

- No merger agreement, support agreement, indenture, credit agreement amendment or financing commitment is supplied, so the finding that creditor change-of-control protection is waived rests on the filings' description and not on the executed terms.

- The consortium is described differently across filings (with and without TWG Global), so the conclusion on who the future sponsor is stays partly open until the merger documents or a later filing settle it.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The pending take-private is an Agreement and Plan of Merger signed on 9 February 2026 with Madison Parent Inc. and Madison Merger Sub Inc., vehicles of an investor consortium of affiliates and funds advised by Mubadala Capital. Stockholders approve USD 2.43 per share in cash, the antitrust waiting period expired on 9 April 2026, stockholders voted yes on 12 May 2026, and completion still needs regulatory approvals including review by the interagency committee on foreign investment. The company has to pay a USD 39.8 million fee in some terminations, or USD 19.9 million if a superior proposal arrives during the go-shop, and the acquirer would pay USD 92.9 million in others. The outside date is 9 November 2026, extendable to 9 February 2027, and the documents supplied stop before it. The acquirer's equity and debt financing, sources and uses and any ratings effect are not in the documents supplied.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cco-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation C11; calculation C2

The only new debt in the period supplied is the August 2025 refinancing, which replaced USD 2,000.0 million of secured notes due 2027 and 2028 with USD 2,050.0 million of secured notes due 2031 and 2033, extending the earliest note maturity to 2028, with USD 62.4 million of premium and fees. In 2026 the company obtained consents instead of issuing: the secured notes indentures, the senior secured credit agreement and the receivables-based credit agreement were amended so that the Merger is not a change of control, and conditional redemption notices were issued for the 2028 and 2029 senior notes. The first group of amendments is effective but operative only on completion, while the receivables facility amendment, which extends maturity to five years from completion and lifts commitments to USD 250.0 million, takes effect on completion.
Basis: calculation C7; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 102; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cco-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cco-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 34

The company has sold its businesses in Mexico, Peru and Chile, the Europe-North segment for a purchase price of USD 625.0 million and net proceeds of USD 572.0 million, and Brazil for about USD 15.0 million, and on 4 August 2026 it completed the Spain sale for about USD 132.3 million, with net proceeds not yet stated and intended for debt reduction subject to the Merger. These sales left the company a focused United States business and are the source of its deleveraging in 2025.
Basis: calculation C6; calculation C10; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 94; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cco-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 9

# Fundamental credit: Clear Channel Outdoor Holdings, Inc. (cco), as of 2026-11-05
## Request

Fundamental credit synthesis of Clear Channel Outdoor Holdings, Inc. (issuer id cco), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the business, financial profile, refinancing capacity, downside and monitoring view for creditors, from the seven supplied documents and the three accepted earlier analyses.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended 31 December 2025 | 2026-02-26 | 571124584b3bbe99a4fbff8adfaba5f0fb8933c5a0003d1ef35708c36c286d39 | Business model, competitive forces, risk factors, Merger terms, debt notes, covenants, maturity ladder |

## Findings
### Bottom line

The fundamental credit profile is weak on leverage but supported by a regulated, growing outdoor advertising business, so creditors depend on refinancing the 2028 and 2029 maturities and on how the pending take-private is financed, not on cash generation.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C8

Total debt is 9.38x Adjusted EBITDA and cash interest absorbs 71.67% of that EBITDA, so a fall of 15.48% in Adjusted EBITDA would remove free cash flow. Liquidity of about USD 398 million covers the USD 197 million of cash interest due in the second half of 2026 twice over, and no debt matures before 2028. Net debt of about USD 4.9 billion is not pro forma for the Spain sale completed on 4 August 2026, whose effect on net debt is not established.
Basis: calculation C3; calculation C1; calculation C7; Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Key findings

- Leverage, not liquidity, is the binding constraint. Total debt is 9.38x Adjusted EBITDA and 10.46x reported EBITDA, cash interest of about USD 390 million costs 7.64% of debt and absorbs 71.67% of Adjusted EBITDA, and free cash flow after interest and capital expenditure is only about USD 84 million. A fall of 15.48% in Adjusted EBITDA removes it, and a fall of 28.33% leaves earnings equal to cash interest. Debt barely moved (up 0.09% from year-end 2025), so the improvement from 10.11x came from earnings and stays hostage to the advertising cycle, not to repayment.
Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C14; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- The 2028 and 2029 maturities decide the credit, and the Merger can move them either way. Maturities of about USD 2.2 billion fall due in those two years, 43.33% of principal, starting with the 2028 senior notes about 17 months after the as-of date. About USD 1.8 billion of unsecured 2028 and 2029 notes carry conditional redemption notices that bite only if the Merger completes. If the acquirer retires them with equity, refinancing risk falls; if it funds the redemption with secured debt, the secured share of principal, now 64.87%, rises and the secured claim grows ahead of what remains. The financing is not disclosed, so the direction is not established.
Basis: calculation C8; calculation C9; calculation C16; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-06-30_cco-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cco-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 34

- Business quality is better than the capital structure it carries. The company is a regulated United States outdoor operator whose revenue grew 6.57% in 2025 and 10.17% in the first half of 2026, with digital displays at 44.1% of revenue and an Adjusted EBITDA margin of 32.41%. Barriers to new inventory and exclusive airport and street furniture contracts protect the franchise, but site leases cost 38.91% of revenue and are partly fixed minimums, so profit moves by more than sales when demand turns.

Basis: calculation C14; calculation C18; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 57; Business & governance (CP-1A)

- Earnings quality and leases qualify the headline leverage. Adjusted EBITDA is 11.50% above reported EBITDA and its last twelve months include a calculated quarter, so the 10.46x reported ratio is the more demanding read. Operating lease liabilities equal 26.66% of total debt and sit outside the debt ratios, so the true fixed-charge burden is heavier than any ratio shown.
Basis: calculation C13; calculation C15; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Liquidity is adequate for about a year, not for a prolonged downturn. Cash and undrawn facilities of about USD 398 million cover second-half 2026 cash interest 2.02x but 2027 cash interest of about USD 394 million only 1.01x, and receivables availability is limited by a borrowing base. A first lien leverage covenant of 7.10x applies only if the revolver is drawn or undrawn letters of credit exceed USD 10 million, and its headroom cannot be calculated here. A fall of 20% in Adjusted EBITDA would turn free cash flow negative at about USD 25 million with cover of 1.12x.
Basis: calculation C7; calculation C5; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cco-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cco-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 109

- Financial policy has favoured creditors, but control is about to change. No dividend has been paid, disposal proceeds prepaid the term loan of a former subsidiary and notes were bought back at a discount, yet the cost of debt rose in the 2025 refinancing and the creditor consents to the Merger remove change-of-control protection. The acquirer's behaviour cannot be inferred from its identity, so the governance assessment stays at average with high uncertainty.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 73; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 102; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cco-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case for a better view is that earnings are compounding while debt is flat: revenue grew 10.17% in the first half of 2026 and Adjusted EBITDA for the last twelve months is 7.82% above 2025, no debt matures for about 17 months, and the Merger arrives with creditor consents, a receivables facility to be extended to five years from completion and conditional redemption notices already issued for USD 1.8 billion of unsecured notes. If earnings kept growing at the recent pace with debt unchanged, leverage would keep falling without any refinancing.
Basis: calculation C14; calculation C9; calculation C16; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cco-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; Business & governance (CP-1A)

The view would improve if the acquirer disclosed financing that retires the unsecured notes with equity and leaves secured debt unchanged, if leverage fell below 9.00x on reported earnings, or if cash interest cover rose above 1.50x on Adjusted EBITDA. It would worsen if revenue or margin turned down so that Adjusted EBITDA fell by 15.48% or more, if the Merger failed with the 2028 notes still unrefinanced, or if the acquirer funded redemption with debt ranking ahead of the notes it replaced.
Basis: calculation C1; calculation C5; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Limitations

- No management forecast, guidance or analyst projection is supplied, so the 15.48% and 28.33% cushions and the 10% and 20% sensitivities are analyst assumptions that hold interest, tax, working capital and lease payments at last-twelve-month levels; real outcomes will differ, and the margin of safety could be smaller if costs are stickier than assumed.
Basis: calculation C5; calculation C6; Source readiness (CP-0)

- No peer set, rating action or market price is supplied, so the comparison with typical high yield outdoor and media issuers rests on judgement, and the weak liquidity-to-maturity coverage cannot be tested against what the market would charge to refinance.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0)

- The latest balance sheet is 30 June 2026, four months before the as-of date, and cash interest of USD 197 million and USD 394 million assumes no refinancing, so the near-term liquidity conclusion could change if the Merger completed or failed after the last document.

- Covenant definitions and compliance workings are not supplied, so the conclusion that near-term liquidity is adequate does not extend to covenant capacity; the first lien leverage test is stated but its headroom is not calculable.

- The term loan's maturity of 23 August 2028 is subject to a springing test on secured notes outstanding above USD 250 million on 15 May 2027 or above USD 199 million on 15 January 2028, and the annual report does not name those notes. The secured notes redeemed in August 2025 had earlier maturities, so the test may now be moot, but the filing does not say so; if it applied the USD 425 million term loan could fall due in 2027 and the conclusion that nothing matures before 2028 would change.
### Fundamental credit drivers
The table sets the latest leverage, cover, cash flow and liquidity against the prior year-end and shows that earnings growth, not repayment, drove the improvement.
| Driver | Latest, LTM to 2026-06-30 | Prior, FY2025 | Change | Consequence for creditors | Source |
| Total debt / Adjusted EBITDA | 9.38x | 10.11x | Lower | Still very high; refinancing dependent | Financial foundation (CP-1) |
| Total debt / reported EBITDA | 10.46x | 10.51x | Slightly lower | Demanding read of leverage | Financial foundation (CP-1) |
| Adjusted EBITDA / cash interest | 1.40x | 1.28x | Higher | Thin cover; shortfall falls on liquidity | Financial foundation (CP-1) |
| Free cash flow after interest and capex | USD 84 million | USD 32 million | Higher | Small cushion against an earnings fall | Financial foundation (CP-1) |
| Cash and undrawn facilities | USD 398 million | USD 396 million | Flat | About a year of cash interest | Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_cco-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 33 |
| Maturities in 2028 and 2029 | USD 2.2 billion | Not applicable | Not applicable | Largest credit event | Financial foundation (CP-1) |
| Adjusted EBITDA margin | 32.41% | 31.47% | Higher | Margin gains support cover | Financial foundation (CP-1) |
| Revenue growth | 10.17% (H1 2026) | 6.57% (FY2025) | Higher | Demand firm; cycle risk remains | Financial foundation (CP-1) |
### Strengths and weaknesses

The main credit strengths are a regulated franchise, rising earnings and enough near-term liquidity. Barriers to new billboard inventory and exclusive airport and street furniture contracts protect pricing, so revenue grew 6.57% in 2025; digital conversion lifted the digital share to 44.1% and the Adjusted EBITDA margin to 32.41%; and cash and undrawn facilities of about USD 398 million cover cash interest for the rest of 2026 twice over with no maturity before 2028. Creditors also benefit from a record of no dividends, disposal proceeds applied to debt and, until the Merger closes, a bar on new borrowing and distributions.
Basis: calculation C14; calculation C7; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 57; Business & governance (CP-1A)

The main weaknesses are leverage, concentrated maturities and a fixed cost base. Total debt is 9.38x Adjusted EBITDA with only 1.40x cover, so a fall of 15.48% in Adjusted EBITDA removes free cash flow; USD 2.2 billion falls due in 2028 and 2029 with the buyer's financing undisclosed; and site leases cost 38.91% of revenue, partly in fixed minimums, with operating lease liabilities of 26.66% of debt outside the ratios. On the nine dimensions of the financial profile, scale and competitive advantage are average, diversification is weak, cost flexibility and free cash flow stability are weak, margin stability is average, refinancing access and liquidity are average, and financial policy and governance are average pending the change of control.
Basis: calculation C1; calculation C8; calculation C18; calculation C15; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Company and ownership

The company sells advertising on roadside billboards, street furniture and airport displays, almost entirely in the United States, and about 75% of revenue comes from the America segment and about 25% from Airports. Most advertising is sold in four-week periods, so revenue reprices quickly in both directions, while contracts for sites, street furniture and airports run for years with minimum fees, so costs are slow to move. The mix gives short revenue visibility and a long fixed commitment, which is why modest revenue declines hit free cash flow quickly.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation C18; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Ownership is dispersed today and passes to an acquirer vehicle on completion of the Merger, with funds advised by Mubadala Capital named as the consortium and TWG Global named in earlier documents but not in the latest. Creditors consented to amendments that make the Merger not a change of control, so they hold no takeover put, and the sponsor's willingness to support the credit is not evidenced; no sponsor history, equity cure or parent guarantee is supplied.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-06-30_cco-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cco-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17
### Revenue, costs and cash conversion

Revenue is recurring in character but not contractual in the short run: advertising spend follows economic conditions, is sold mostly in four-week blocks and shows no single advertiser as material, so demand is diversified but reprices fast. Airports revenue depends on air travel demand and America on local market conditions, so a downturn reaches revenue within a quarter. The credit consequence is stable medium-term revenue with high sensitivity to the cycle in any single year.

Site leases, which cost 38.91% of revenue, combine minimum payments with revenue sharing, so margin is defended only partly when volume falls; the Adjusted EBITDA margin of 32.41% would compress faster than revenue if costs are as fixed as the contracts suggest, and the two bounds of 5.02% and 15.48% for the revenue fall that removes free cash flow show how wide that uncertainty is. Capital expenditure of 3.85% of revenue in 2025 is a flexible lever, because digital conversions are discretionary, but cutting it slows the growth that supports the margin.
Basis: calculation C18; calculation C6; calculation C11; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 64; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 65

Conversion of Adjusted EBITDA into free cash flow is low: 6.34% in 2025 and 15.48% in the last twelve months, because cash interest takes 71.67% of EBITDA before capital expenditure, tax and working capital. That leaves almost nothing for debt reduction, so deleveraging must come from earnings growth or asset sales; cash flows combine continuing and discontinued operations, which could overstate the continuing business's conversion.
Basis: calculation C12; calculation C3; Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Competitive forces and external factors

Rivalry is moderate: the United States outdoor industry is fragmented, with Lamar and Outfront among its other large operators and many local ones, and competition turns on audience reach, location quality and measurable results; the company can manage rates when demand rises because inventory is limited, which supports margin in an upswing but gives no protection in a downturn. New entrants face high barriers, because federal, state and local rules limit new billboard inventory and airport, transit and street furniture rights sit in exclusive contracts, which supports franchise value and recovery prospects but exposes the company to rebid risk when contracts expire. Substitutes are the main long-run threat, since outdoor advertising is only 2.3% of United States advertising spend and competes with digital media, while an outside forecast the company cites expects outdoor revenue to grow 4.0% a year from 2026 to 2030. Buyers are diversified and short-term, which lowers concentration risk and shortens visibility; suppliers, meaning landlords and authorities, hold the stronger hand because lease and concession cost is a very large expense and partly fixed.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 32; calculation C18

Political and regulatory factors matter because billboard control laws, possible taxes on outdoor revenue and review of the Merger by the interagency committee on foreign investment shape inventory, cost and the timing of the take-private; economic factors matter most, because advertising spend follows output and borrowing costs remain elevated. Social and technology factors are not primary credit drivers: digital conversion needs capital expenditure but the filings do not show it threatening the franchise.

In credit terms the strengths are a protected franchise, growing digital revenue, firm recent growth and adequate near-term liquidity; the weaknesses are high leverage, thin cover, a fixed cost base and a concentrated refinancing wall. The opportunities are digital conversion, Airports growth and, if the Merger completes with equity, a lighter unsecured stack; the threats are an advertising downturn, falling air travel, failure to refinance 2028 and an acquirer that adds secured debt.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6
### Outlook

Over the next twelve to twenty-four months the near-term outlook is supportive but unproven: first-half revenue growth of 10.17% and rising margin favour a further fall in leverage if debt stays flat, no debt matures, and the Merger caps new borrowing until it closes; headwinds are the cash cost of the Merger, a seasonally weak first quarter that leaves debt service resting on the lowest earnings of the year, and elevated interest rates. Over three to five years the outlook depends on the 2028 and 2029 refinancing and on whether the acquirer adds or removes debt; a sector tailwind is the outside forecast of 4.0% annual growth in outdoor revenue to 2030, which is the company's cited view and not tested here. The company gives no guidance, so the outlook is an analyst reading.
Basis: calculation C14; calculation C16; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; Source readiness (CP-0)
### Downside scenario

A realistic downside starts with an advertising slowdown that cuts revenue across both segments and a fall in air travel that hits Airports. Because most advertising is sold in four-week blocks, revenue falls within a quarter, while site lease minimums and concession fees do not, so Adjusted EBITDA falls by more than revenue; a fall of 15.48% in Adjusted EBITDA removes free cash flow, and a fall of 20% turns it negative at about USD 25 million with cover of 1.12x. The gap is funded from cash and undrawn availability of about USD 398 million, which lasts about one year of cash interest, so liquidity is not distressed in 2027 but the 2028 notes would have to be refinanced with cover near 1.12x, at a time when the cost of that debt is likely higher than the average of 7.64%. Management can cut capital expenditure, which was 3.85% of revenue in 2025, and apply Spain proceeds to debt, subject to the Merger. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress through 2027 but not sufficient to refinance 2028 on current terms without a recovery or sponsor support.
Basis: calculation C5; calculation C7; calculation C11; calculation C6; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cco-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 9
### Overall credit view

Overall, Clear Channel Outdoor Holdings presents an adequate business profile supported by a regulated United States franchise, rising digital revenue and firm recent growth, but credit quality is constrained by leverage of 9.38x Adjusted EBITDA and thin cash interest cover of 1.40x. Cash-flow durability appears weak because free cash flow is about USD 84 million, which a fall of 15.48% in Adjusted EBITDA removes. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on earnings growth, on whether the Merger completes and on how the acquirer finances the redemption of the 2028 and 2029 unsecured notes. The primary downside path is an advertising downturn that reaches earnings through fixed site costs and meets the 2028 maturities with little cushion. Further analysis would require the acquirer's financing, a management projection and covenant workings. Top risk: refinancing the 2028 and 2029 maturities after an earnings downturn.
Basis: calculation C1; calculation C8; calculation C5; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)
